q-eh-09.Decks and appurtenant railings: A deck can feel like optional outdoor furniture, yet NC lists decks, balconies, stoops, and their railings among required exterior items.

q-fp-02.It mainly weakens the draft, so smoke ma: Draft is set mostly by the flue and damper above, not by small gaps in the firebox lining below.

q-fp-03.Leave it alone; dampers are outside the: InterNACHI's fireplace section does name the damper door. A visual inspection is not purely hands-off for every fireplace part.

q-fp-05.A Level I visual inspection by the homeo: A Level I look covers only easily reached chimney parts, the same limit your own SOP already has. Ask whether that fills any gap.

q-fp-07.It is decorative trim that hides the top: Work at a chimney top is costly to build and maintain, so little up there exists only to hide brick. Ask what job it does.

q-fp-08.Nothing; caps are decorative and optiona: A cap may be optional, but optional does not mean useless. Ask whether the client gains anything from knowing it is missing.

q-hv-02.Upward toward the chimney at least 1 in: The figure in this option is larger than the usual code minimum. Recheck the number, and separately recheck which way the pipe should run.

q-hv-06.The smaller liquid line, since it carrie: The liquid line leaves the condenser after it has shed its heat, so it usually feels warm rather than cold.

q-hv-07.It is cosmetic, though the pad should be: Cosmetic means appearance only. A machine that runs for years at a tilt raises a function question, so ask what the tilt affects.

q-hv-10.Returns are mostly decorative grilles th: Each return grille connects through ductwork to the air handler. A grille meant just for looks would not need a duct behind it.

q-wh-01.12 in: Recall the exact figure your plumbing sources give for TPR discharge termination height, rather than estimating from what seems like a sensible height.

q-wh-03.The cold water inlet is at the top of th: The cold inlet fitting is often on top, but a dip tube carries that incoming water down near the bottom of the tank.

q-wh-04.Cold water hitting the hot steel cracks: Steel bends and tears rather than shattering, and cold water already enters a hot tank through the dip tube every time a tap runs.

q-wh-05.You are required to estimate the remaini: Estimating years left would be a prediction. Ask whether NC lists that among the items it obliges you to report.
q-wh-05.You are required to recommend replacing: A 2001 date tells you age, not condition. Ask whether NC makes age by itself a reason you must call for replacement.
q-wh-05.You may not mention the age, since that: Stating a manufacture date is a fact read off a label, not a forecast of when the heater will fail.

q-wh-09.Yes, if the client is present to watch t: Ask whether the client's presence appears anywhere in NC's plumbing rules as a condition for testing a valve.

q-mo-02.That the insulation above that spot is m: Missing insulation reads warm, not cool, on a ceiling under a hot summer attic. Ask what season and conditions this image came from.

q-mo-05.It mainly affects how the grout looks al: Caulk and grout are separate materials, and a gap in the caulk does not change how the neighboring grout looks.

q-mo-07.Condensation from the tank on a humid da: Condensation forms on the outside of the porcelain, so you would expect beads of water on the tank and bowl, not only at the base.
q-mo-07.A clogged vent stack forcing water back: A blocked vent usually shows up as slow drains, gurgling, or traps losing water, not as a wet floor at a single fixture.

q-mo-08.As mold growth that needs remediation by: Dark staining on crawlspace wood can come from water, tannins, or growth, and only lab sampling identifies a growth.
q-mo-08.As acceptable, since crawlspace wood oft: Typical crawlspace framing reads well under 20 percent. Ask whether 24 percent is typical, and what sustained dampness does to wood.

q-mo-10.The two stains are unrelated, and each o: Review what NC and InterNACHI say about attic inspection, and what a report should do with active water stains.

q-ai-01.Its chemical composition and fire rating: Chemical makeup and fire ratings come from lab testing. Ask whether the SOP's insulation wording asks you for test results.

q-ai-02.Nothing, because NC excludes measuring R: The R-value exclusion stops you from measuring or calculating thermal resistance. It does not tell you to stay silent about the attic.

q-ai-04.Hold the insulation tight against the ro: Attic insulation rests on the ceiling by gravity at the eaves; it does not need a part to press it up against the roof deck.

q-ai-10.Repair item; recommend sanding and repai: Edge paint wears where a door brushes its frame in daily use. Ask whether NC expects you to recommend paint touch-ups.

q-ai-11.Nothing more; a fan that pulls air is wo: One passing test seldom finishes an inspection item. Ask what else about a bath fan you would still want to check.

q-dk-01.Monitor it, unless the ledger is visibly: Nailed ledgers often look snug until they let go, so visible pulling is a poor early warning sign.

q-dk-02.To keep termites and carpenter ants out: Insects reach wood from the soil and through cracks. A strip along the ledger top is a poor place for a pest barrier.
q-dk-02.To stop the ledger from swelling and exp: A thin strip lapped over the ledger cannot restrain wood movement, and heat expansion in lumber is minor anyway.

q-dk-03.Brick is acceptable as long as the throu: Galvanizing addresses rust on the bolt. Ask whether corrosion is really the concern this question raises.
q-dk-03.Bolts through brick hold better than lag: How well a fastener holds depends on more than its type. Comparing bolts with lags does not explain why this setup is a problem.
q-dk-03.It is a cosmetic concern, since the mort: Cosmetic means appearance only. Ask whether a question about how a deck is attached is mainly about looks.

q-dk-06.Above 48 in, measured at the deck's oute: 48 in is a figure some people carry over from other rules. The deck guard trigger is a lower height.

q-rf-06.Extend 1 ft above the landing, 1 ft out: One foot above the landing leaves almost nothing to hold on to while stepping on or off the ladder.

q-rf-08.Antennae, satellite dishes, and their ro: Reread InterNACHI 3.1 twice: once for what you shall inspect, once for what you are not required to inspect.
q-rf-08.Lightning arrestors and their ground wir: Compare each option against the two lists in InterNACHI 3.1: the items you shall inspect and the items set aside.
q-rf-08.De-icing cables along the eaves and gutt: Recall the InterNACHI 3.1 roof section as two lists, required and not required, and place each option on one.

q-ra-01.Bond the shingles together into one seal: Shingles bond to each other through a factory sealant strip, not through the loose granules on their faces.
q-ra-01.Make the shingle waterproof, so underlay: The asphalt itself is the water-shedding part of a shingle, and underlayment is called for under shingles regardless.

q-ra-08.A third layer is fine if longer nails re: Review the rules for roofing over existing shingles taught in the 25 Standards course before choosing among the remaining options.
q-ra-08.Re-covering is better, since the old lay: Asphalt shingles add very little insulating value; a layer of them insulates about as much as thin plywood.
q-ra-08.Layer count does not matter for asphalt: Review what the 25 Standards course teaches about roofing over an existing asphalt roof before choosing again.

q-fd-02.It is typical shrinkage of block walls a: Curing shrinkage happens in the first months after construction and leaves fine hairline cracks, usually in the mortar joints.

q-fd-03.Mold growth on the block; recommend prof: Mold needs organic food, and bare concrete block offers very little. Also recall that NC excludes determining mold.

q-fd-04.Monitor it, since the pier is not leanin: Leaning is a late sign. A crack through the blocks themselves, not just the mortar joints, tells you something before any lean.

q-fd-07.The depth and width of the footings belo: Footings sit below grade, and NC does not require you to dig or move soil to reach hidden parts.
q-fd-07.The compressive strength of the foundati: Concrete strength comes from lab tests on cylinders or cores, and the SOP excludes calculating strength or adequacy.
q-fd-07.The soil type and its bearing capacity b: Soil bearing capacity comes from geotechnical testing, and NC also excludes geological and soil conditions.

q-fd-08.Calculate the load on the pier to judge: NC lists calculating the strength or adequacy of a system among the things inspectors are not required to do.

q-rt-01.Lift a few tiles to see the condition of: Seeing the underlayment means removing roof covering, which goes beyond what NC asks an inspector to expose.

q-rt-02.It is cosmetic, since tile is mostly the: Clay tile is costly and heavy. Few owners would carry that load on their framing for appearance alone.
q-rt-02.Cracked tile still sheds water; replace: Replacing at resale ties the repair to a sale date. Ask whether the roof's condition follows that schedule.

q-rt-03.The roof slope is too steep to hold the: Tile is routinely installed on steep slopes, and a slope problem would affect the whole roof, not just the eave tiles.

q-rt-04.The mortar packed between the tiles at t: Mortar is porous and cracks with movement, and it is used mainly to bed hip and ridge tiles, not to seal field laps.

q-rt-06.Major defect; mortar fails over time: Even when mortar needs attention, the label major is kept for serious conditions such as structural or safety issues.

q-rt-07.It may not be inspected, even if the cli: An SOP sets a minimum for an inspection. Ask whether a minimum also forbids doing anything beyond it.

q-rt-08.The underlayment needs upgrading, but no: Review what the 25 Standards course says about changing roof covering types on existing framing before choosing again.
q-rt-08.Tile is lighter than asphalt, so framing: Look up typical installed weights per square for clay tile and asphalt shingles, then reread the remaining options.

q-eg-07.A door from the garage into an inside ha: Garage doors into hallways are common and allowed when the door meets the fire-separation rules for that opening.

q-pl-01.It wastes water each time the fixture is: Water use is set by the faucet and how long it runs, not by the shape of the trap below.

q-pl-03.Yes, cycle each stop to prove it shuts o: Thoroughness is good, but ask whether your SOP's plumbing section lists stop valves among the things you operate.
q-pl-03.Yes, but just the hot side, where scale: Scale does build on hot lines, but that makes an old hot stop more likely to stick or leak, not less.
q-pl-03.Yes, if the client asks you to check the: Ask whether your SOP ties what you operate to client requests, or to a fixed list in its plumbing section.

q-pl-04.It matters at bathroom sinks, not at the: Ask whether drain material rules in model plumbing codes change from one room's sink to another's.

q-pl-06.Report it as polybutylene, a known failu: Polybutylene and PEX are both flexible plastic, but they are different materials with different markings and track records.
q-pl-06.Recommend replacing it with galvanized s: Galvanized steel corrodes inside over time. It is the material many older houses are replacing, not a modern upgrade.

q-pl-08.Acceptable, since toilets can rock a lit: Toilets are designed to sit firm on the floor. Ask whether any rocking at all is a normal design condition.
q-pl-08.Cosmetic, once the caulk at the base is: Caulk at the base holds nothing down. Ask whether fresh caulk would stop the movement you felt.
q-pl-08.Tighten the flange bolts yourself and mo: Tightening bolts is a repair. Ask whether repairs are part of a home inspector's role during an inspection.

q-st-01.Repair it by nailing a scrap board over: Repairs are outside a home inspector's role, and you would own whatever your fix did to the house.

q-st-06.Joists to piers to girder to footings to: Sketch the crawlspace framing from the floor surface downward, drawing each member where it sits, before choosing again.

q-st-08.The adequacy of the foundation anchor bo: Reread InterNACHI 3.3 and list what it says you shall report, then compare each option to that list.
q-st-08.The load capacity of each floor joist an: Recall the exact items InterNACHI 3.3 tells you to report, and check each remaining option against them.
